mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened financial conditions and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS increase is ≤0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 jobs coinciding with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as labor market strength supports corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 and UNRATE falls below 4.5% in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening with low unemployment
failure_condition: Across 12 consecutive months of such labor conditions, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of neutral returns (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 10% followed within two months by a rise in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) above 1,500 units predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as a leading indicator of economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥10% in month t and HOUST increases by ≥1,500 units in month t+1
regime_hint: Early-stage industrial and consumer demand acceleration
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative or indistinguishable from zero when INDPRO growth is not accompanied by the specified HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in inflation (CPIAUCSL) of at least 2% over two months while industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat suggests supply-side easing, which is expected to produce a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥2% over two consecutive months and INDPRO is flat in both months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative or the pattern of disinflation is not confirmed by a 5% or greater out-of-sample Sharpe ratio improvement over the prior 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) without a corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE), a persistent decline in the 3-month moving average of the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected, indicating a risk-off environment from persistent deflationary expectations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for 3 consecutive months while UNRATE remains below 7% over the same period
regime_hint: Deflationary expectations without labor market weakness
failure_condition: Over 12 such months, the 20-day forward return exhibits a positive or statistically significant upward trend (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 100,000 jobs in a month triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as market participants anticipate future earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >100,000 in a single month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (IC < 0.05) when the payroll spike is not followed by a positive market reaction within 2 days.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer confidence (measured by HOUST) falls by more than 200 units in a month while industrial production (INDPRO) remains above 100 (index units), the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a negative 60-day forward return as a sign of weakening demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by >200 units in month t and INDPRO > 100 in the same month
failure_condition: Over 10 such months, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A long-term upward trend in the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted when the 12-month moving average of GDP deflator inflation (CPIAUCSL) shows a positive slope, indicating structural disinflation and improved investor sentiment over time.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a flat-trend baseline (IC < 0.10) over a 48-month window of observation.
